plan: Given the common knowledge of rationality, the optimal bidding strategy converges towards bidding your true value minus a small amount. This is because bidding too high risks overpaying, while bidding too low risks losing the item even when it's worth more than the bid. Since this is round 1 and there is no previous history, I will bid slightly below my value to attempt to win at a reasonable price. I will bid $24.5.

Given the common knowledge of rationality, the optimal bidding strategy converges to bidding your true value minus a small increment. This is because any bid above your value risks winning at a loss, and any bid significantly below your value risks losing to a slightly lower bid. Since this is round 1 and there's no history, I'll bid slightly below my value to increase the chance of winning at a profit. I'll bid $16.7.

Given the common knowledge of rationality and a single round, the optimal bidding strategy converges to bidding slightly above the expected value of the second highest bid. Since values are between $0 and $49, the expected value of the highest of the other two bids is approximately (2/3)*49 = $32.67. To maximize profit, I'll bid slightly above this, accounting for the $0.1 increment. A bid of $33 seems reasonable.
